questions.q: A survey of $100$ students asks whether they prefer online or in-person learning: 60 are High Schoolers (40 online, 20 in-person) and 40 are Middle Schoolers (15 online, 25 in-person). What fraction of all students surveyed prefer online learning?
questions.answer: Total preferring online: $40 + 15 = 55$. Total students: $100$. Fraction: $\frac{55}{100} = \frac{11}{20}$.

questions.q: In the same survey, what is the probability that a student chosen at random is a Middle School student who prefers in-person learning?
questions.answer: Middle school in-person count is $25$. Out of $100$ total students: $\frac{25}{100} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.q: A hospital clinic logs 120 patients: 70 adults (30 tested positive) and 50 children (20 tested positive). What is the probability that a randomly chosen patient tested negative?

sections.heading: Section 2: Conditional Probability from Frequency Tables

questions.q: From the student survey (60 High School: 40 online, 20 in-person; 40 Middle School: 15 online, 25 in-person), given that a randomly chosen student prefers online learning, what is the probability that the student is in High School?
questions.answer: Condition is 'prefers online' (total $= 40 + 15 = 55$). Among those, $40$ are High School. Probability $= \frac{40}{55} = \frac{8}{11}$.

questions.q: Given that a student is in Middle School, what is the probability that they prefer in-person learning?
questions.answer: Condition is 'Middle School' (total $= 40$). Among Middle Schoolers, $25$ prefer in-person. Probability $= \frac{25}{40} = \frac{5}{8}$.

questions.q: At a conference, 80 attendees are engineers (50 use Python) and 40 are managers (10 use Python). Given that an attendee uses Python, what is the probability that they are an engineer?
questions.answer: Total Python users $= 50 + 10 = 60$. Engineers who use Python $= 50$. Probability $= \frac{50}{60} = \frac{5}{6}$.

questions.q: Events $A$ and $B$ are independent. If $P(A) = 0.40$ and $P(B) = 0.60$, what is $P(A \text{ and } B)$?
questions.answer: For independent events, $P(A \text{ and } B) = P(A) \times P(B) = 0.40 \times 0.60 = 0.24$.

questions.q: A jar contains $6$ red marbles and $4$ blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn at random without replacement. What is the probability that both marbles are red?
questions.answer: First marble red: $\frac{6}{10}$. Second marble red: $\frac{5}{9}$. Combined probability $= \frac{6}{10} \times \frac{5}{9} = \frac{30}{90} = \frac{1}{3}$.

questions.q: If $P(A) = 0.5$, $P(B) = 0.7$, and $P(A \text{ and } B) = 0.35$, which of the following is true?
questions.answer: $P(A) \times P(B) = 0.5 \times 0.7 = 0.35 = P(A \text{ and } B)$. Since the product equals the intersection, $A$ and $B$ are independent.

questions.q: A standard six-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling an even number OR a number greater than $4$?
questions.answer: Even numbers: $\{2, 4, 6\}$ (count 3). Numbers $> 4$: $\{5, 6\}$ (count 2). Union is $\{2, 4, 5, 6\}$ (count 4). Probability $= \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$.

questions.q: If $P(A) = 0.65$, $P(B) = 0.45$, and $P(A \text{ and } B) = 0.25$, what is $P(A \text{ or } B)$?
questions.answer: Addition rule: $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) = 0.65 + 0.45 - 0.25 = 0.85$.

questions.q: In a group of $50$ students, $30$ play soccer, $25$ play basketball, and $10$ play both sports. How many students play neither sport?
questions.answer: Students playing at least one sport: $30 + 25 - 10 = 45$. Students playing neither: $50 - 45 = 5$.
